name: record-row-action
description: The last column of a record listing: one ghost icon button that opens the row's record. Pins itself to the right edge of the scrollport when the table overflows horizontally, on an overlay surface with a shadow, revealed by row hover or focus on fine pointers and always visible on coarse ones. Exports RecordRowAction (the cell) and RecordRowActionHeading (its header cell). Renders exactly one action — there is no overflow menu in this system.

gaps.container: 0 — the container centres a single child

container.note: Applied only when the table overflows; inline tables render an unstyled flex container.
container.pairedSurface: color/surface/overlay and color/surface/overlay/foreground are a pair — never set one without the other. The container floats above rows whose background it does not control.

heading.note: Applied only when the table overflows.
heading.reason: Matches the header row, which already renders surface/raised, so the pin is invisible until a row scrolls under it.

composition.assembly: RecordRowAction renders a TableCell; RecordRowActionHeading renders a TableHead. They are used as a pair in the same Table.
composition.structure: TableCell[data-record-row-action] → div[data-record-action-container] → Button variant=ghost size=icon asChild → next/link → Eye
composition.dataAttributes: data-record-row-action and data-record-action-container carry no styling. They exist so a screen audit can find every instance in rendered DOM — which is how two hand-rolled copies were found in the prototype.
composition.placement: Last column only, with RecordRowActionHeading in the header row. One without the other misaligns the columns.

behavior.overflowDetection: useTableOverflow() from components/ui/table.tsx. The caller cannot force either appearance — two listings side by side would otherwise disagree about whether the action floats.
behavior.pinned: sticky right-0 z-10 with the overlay surface and shadow.
behavior.hoverReveal: Progressive enhancement, and must stay that way. The cell renders opacity-100 and pointer-events-auto; only @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) opts into hiding it, revealed by tr:hover and tr:focus-within. Inverting this makes the action unreachable by touch and keyboard.
behavior.clickIsolation: The link calls event.stopPropagation(). These listings make the whole row clickable with useRowClick; without the stop, the row handler would also fire and the two could disagree about the destination.
behavior.motion: None bound. The reveal is an opacity change with no declared transition.

accessibility.accessibleName: the label prop, as both aria-label and title. The Eye icon is aria-hidden.
accessibility.columnHeader: <th scope='col'> containing visually hidden text 'Open record', so the column is announced rather than read as blank
accessibility.focusIndicator: Button's own ring, not suppressed by the hover reveal
keyboard: Tab reaches the link in row order
tr:focus-within reveals the pinned cell, so tabbing to it never focuses something invisible
accessibility.touch: The hover reveal is behind a fine-pointer media query. Coarse pointers always see the action.

constraints: Always pair RecordRowAction with RecordRowActionHeading in the same table.
Always use it as the last column.
The label must name the record, not the verb alone — 'Open SOP-002 · v3.0', never 'Open'. A screen reader listing the page's links otherwise reads the same word once per row.
Never make this the only route into the record — the record's name in the first column is the primary link.
Never render more than one action from it; it has room for exactly one.
Never override the column width — it is sized to its button plus padding.

useCases: A document or record registry wide enough to scroll horizontally, where the row's name has scrolled out of sight by the time the reader reaches the right edge
A folder listing whose columns vary with content, so overflow cannot be predicted at design time
Any listing already using useRowClick, where a visible affordance is needed to say the row is openable

comparedTo.situation: One row action, and the table may overflow
comparedTo.notInstead: a bare Button in a TableCell

comparedTo.situation: One row action, table can never overflow
comparedTo.notInstead: record-row-action — the hook and overlay buy nothing
record-row-action — it renders exactly one, and no menu exists yet

comparedTo.situation: The action changes the record rather than opening it
comparedTo.use: a button in the row, labelled with the verb
comparedTo.notInstead: record-row-action — the eye icon means view

openQuestions: There is still no row overflow menu in the system. accura-design-patterns.md logs it as a gap and two modules hand-rolled one before this component existed; RecordRowAction renders one action and does not close it. If a menu is built, does it replace this component or sit beside it as a second column?

The pinned appearance has never been audited at 390px. Both consumers were checked on desktop; a narrow viewport, where every table overflows, is the case most likely to look wrong and has not been measured.
notes: Promoted from components/ to components/ui/ on 2026-09-18. Before that it had a story and no meta.json, which is why drift-check rule 5 failed against it.
No Figma node and never had one — it was written in the prototype. Stage 1 of generation-rules.md is a Figma inspection, which does not apply: every token here was read from record-row-action.tsx.
artifactStatus is 'needs review' because the component has not been measured in the browser — not because of any audit process. R1–R8 was retired on 2026-09-18.
changelog: 1.0 (2026-09-18) — first artifact, written on promotion to components/ui/.

darkMode.notes: All four bindings are semantic and mode-aware: surface/overlay, surface/overlay/foreground, surface/raised and shadow/md.
darkMode.pairedSurfaceRisk: surface/overlay must keep its own /foreground. The container floats over rows whose background it does not control, so taking the foreground from the page would invert in dark mode.

notes: Uses next/link, so it is coupled to Next's router in a way the rest of components/ui is not.

storybook.title: Data/RecordRowAction
storybook.notes: Two stories, one per appearance: ScrollableListing forces overflow with min-w-[1000px] in a narrower container; FittingListing renders a table that fits. Title was 'Patterns/RecordRowAction' before promotion — the only Patterns/ entry in the library.
